scenario: Workers plan to enter a storage vessel to clean residues. The vessel last contained flammable solvent. Gas monitor reads 8% LEL. No permit has been issued. One worker is already inside.
expected_decision: STOP WORK — Immediate evacuation required: 8% LEL in confined space with personnel inside; no permit; fire and asphyxiation risk. Evacuate and do not re-enter until atmosphere is cleared and permit issued.
evidence_sources: Hot Work Permit to Work procedure

scenario: Fine-Kinney risk assessment conducted by site HSSE officer gives a score of 540. Expert consultant independently calculated the same scenario and obtained the same result.
expected_decision: STOP WORK — Extreme Risk Level Detected
expert_decision: STOP WORK — Extreme Risk Level Detected

scenario: Worker cutting granite with dry diamond blade for 4 hours. Industrial hygiene monitoring shows silica TWA of 0.07 mg/m³ against OEL of 0.05 mg/m³. Only N95 respirator is provided.
expected_decision: CORRECTIVE ACTION REQUIRED — TWA Exceeds Occupational Exposure Limit

scenario: A worker asks whether it is safe to enter a maintenance pit where a chemical leak occurred earlier. The leak source, chemical identity, and current atmospheric conditions are all unknown.
expected_decision: INSUFFICIENT INFORMATION — Cannot determine safe decision without verified evidence
evidence_sources: Chemical identity must be established before entry assessment

scenario: Electrician working on an 11 kV circuit breaker. LOTO procedure was started but only electrical isolation was applied. Pneumatic actuator on the breaker was not isolated. Worker is about to open the cabinet.
expected_decision: STOP WORK — All energy sources must be isolated and verified at zero energy state before cabinet is opened; LOTO must cover electrical, pneumatic, and stored energy sources
evidence_sources: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 — Control of Hazardous Energy
All energy sources must be isolated

scenario: Crane rigging for offshore module installation. Computed safety factor by rigger is 4.2. Independent check by lifting engineer confirms the same value.
expected_decision: STOP WORK AUTHORITY — Insufficient Safety Factor
expert_decision: STOP WORK AUTHORITY — Insufficient Safety Factor
evidence_sources: ASME B30.9 — minimum SF 5.0 for critical lifts

scenario: Demolition workers are disturbing ceiling tiles in a building constructed in 1978. Asbestos survey has not been conducted.
expected_decision: STOP WORK — Asbestos survey required before any disturbance of suspect materials in buildings built before 1990; potential asbestos-containing materials must be tested before demolition proceeds
